eslint-js/no-restricted-properties.message: Read settings from src/config/env.ts, which parses the environment once at boot (STANDARD.md#config).

patterns.message: Folders reach each other through @/ (or #folder/ in a monorepo), never ../ (STANDARD.md#folders).
Import a workspace package through its public entry, never its internals. Export what you need from the package's index (STANDARD.md#monorepo).
Production code never imports test helpers (STANDARD.md#tests).
Raw runtime modules live behind @/platform. Use or extend a wrapper there (STANDARD.md#platform).
Bun's runtime modules live behind @/platform. Use or extend a wrapper there (STANDARD.md#platform).
Drivers and HTTP clients live behind @/platform. Use @/platform/http or a wrapper there (STANDARD.md#platform).

HttpApiSwagger embeds a 2 MB Swagger UI in the server. Serve docs with HttpApiScalar.layerCdn(Api, { path: "/docs", version: "x.y.z" }), mounted only when docs are enabled (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).

Import each Effect module from its own path: import * as Effect from "effect/Effect", import * as HttpApiBuilder from "effect/http-api/HttpApiBuilder". Barrels like "effect" or "effect/http" pull in every module for bundlers without deep scope analysis (STANDARD.md#effect-imports).
Use the public v4 path: effect/unstable/<module> became effect/<module>, and internals are not part of the API (STANDARD.md#effect-imports).

This is a v3 module. v4 names: Either → effect/Result, FiberRef → Context.Reference, JSONSchema → effect/JsonSchema, TestClock → effect/testing/TestClock, FastCheck → fast-check, Runtime → removed (STANDARD.md#effect-imports).

This v3 package is part of effect in v4: @effect/platform/HttpClient → effect/http/HttpClient, @effect/platform/HttpApi → effect/http-api/HttpApi, @effect/schema → effect/Schema (STANDARD.md#effect-imports).
Effect code validates with Schema: import * as Schema from "effect/Schema". One schema library means one decode path and errors that carry a type (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
In Effect code use effect/Match, effect/Array, effect/Record, effect/Option and effect/Result: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use effect/Schema: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use effect/DateTime and effect/Duration: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use Effect.log*, with the logger chosen in @/platform/log: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use effect/http-api (HttpApi) for HTTP, or effect/rpc for RPC: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use Context.Service and Layer: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).

In Effect code use effect/sql (SqlClient, SqlSchema, Model) with a @effect/sql-* driver in @/platform: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use Effect.retry with Schedule, Effect.forEach({ concurrency }) and Semaphore: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use effect/Stream: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use effect/cli: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
In Effect code use effect/ai with an @effect/ai-* provider layer in @/platform: one library, typed errors in the Effect channel, and testable services (STANDARD.md#effect-libraries).
Runtime, driver and telemetry packages live behind @/platform. Export a Layer (or runMain) from a file there (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Loggers and HTTP client implementations are chosen once in @/platform. Log with Effect.log*, and depend on HttpClient.HttpClient (STANDARD.md#effect-logging).

Endpoints are schema-first: declare one with HttpApiEndpoint in src/data/api and implement it with HttpApiBuilder.group. Hand-written routes skip validation, OpenAPI and the typed client (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).
The HTTP contract (HttpApi, groups, endpoints) lives in src/data/api, separate from the server, so clients can import it without server code (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).

HttpApiScalar.layer embeds the 3.2 MB Scalar app in the server. Use HttpApiScalar.layerCdn(Api, { path: "/docs", version: "x.y.z" }), mounted only when docs are enabled (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).
Pin the Scalar version: HttpApiScalar.layerCdn(Api, { path: "/docs", version: "1.43.5" }). Without it the page loads @scalar/api-reference@latest from jsDelivr (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).
Import the module as a namespace: import * as Effect from "effect/Effect" (or import type * as ...). One import style, and every call reads Module.fn (STANDARD.md#effect-imports).
Use Effect.fn("name")(function* (...) { ... }) instead of a function that only returns Effect.gen. It names the span and keeps stack traces (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Use Effect.fn("name")(function* (...) { ... }) instead of a function that only returns Effect.gen. It names the span and keeps stack traces (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Use Effect.fn("name")(function* (...) { ... }) instead of a function that only returns Effect.gen. It names the span and keeps stack traces (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Do not .pipe an Effect.fn. Pass the combinators as extra arguments: Effect.fn("name")(function* () {...}, Effect.catchTag(...)) (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Do not .pipe an Effect.fn. Pass the combinators as extra arguments: Effect.fn("name")(function* () {...}, Effect.catchTag(...)) (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Name a reusable Effect.fn after its variable: const getUser = Effect.fn("getUser")(function* ...). Use Effect.fnUntraced when it is not a useful tracing span (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Do not throw inside Effect code: a throw becomes an untyped defect. Fail with a typed error: return yield* new SomeError({...}) (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }, { httpApiStatus }). HttpApi can then encode them and the typed client can decode them (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Fail with a Schema.TaggedError, not a bare Error, so callers can catchTag it and HttpApi can map it to a status (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }), not by extending Error (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchAll is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catch (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchAllCause is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchCause (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchAllDefect is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchDefect (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchSome is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchFilter (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchSomeCause is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchCauseFilter (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.fork is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.forkChild (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.forkDaemon is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.forkDetach (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
v4 services use Context.Service<Self, Shape>()("package/path/Name") (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
v4 services use Context.Service<Self, Shape>()("package/path/Name"), with a static layer built by Layer.effect (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Give the service a global identifier with the package and folder path: "my-service/features/prices/Prices" (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Declare the real schema. The endpoint schema validates input, encodes output, and generates OpenAPI and the typed client (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).
Keep the message constant and put values in fields: Effect.logInfo("price served").pipe(Effect.annotateLogs({ ticker })) (STANDARD.md#effect-logging).
Effect.promise turns a rejection into a defect. Wrap the Promise API once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch: (cause) => new SomeError({ cause }) }) (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
The service has one HttpApi, in src/data/api/Api.ts. Add your group to it there (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Groups and endpoints live in src/data/api/<group>/<Group>Api.ts, one group per file (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Errors live in an errors.ts file: src/data/api/<group>/errors.ts for errors on the wire, src/features/<name>/errors.ts for internal ones (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Handlers live in src/features/<group>/handlers.ts, named after the group they implement (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Give every service its production layer as static readonly layer, so src/app wires X.layer and tests swap in another static layer (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once, and tests may run effects. Everywhere else, return the Effect (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
A ManagedRuntime bridges Effect into non-Effect code. Build it once in src/app (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Provide layers once, in src/app. Below it, declare what you need with yield* SomeService and compose layers with Layer.provide (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Promise APIs are wrapped once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise and a tagged error. Call that wrapper here (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Effect code has no async functions. Return an Effect, or wrap the Promise API in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Read configuration in src/config only: expose it as a service with a layer there (AppConfig.layer), and yield* it where it is needed (STANDARD.md#effect-config).

This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).

Groups and endpoints live in src/data/api/<group>/<Group>Api.ts, one group per file (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).

Handlers live in src/features/<group>/handlers.ts, named after the group they implement (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Give every service its production layer as static readonly layer, so src/app wires X.layer and tests swap in another static layer (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once, and tests may run effects. Everywhere else, return the Effect (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
A ManagedRuntime bridges Effect into non-Effect code. Build it once in src/app (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Provide layers once, in src/app. Below it, declare what you need with yield* SomeService and compose layers with Layer.provide (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Promise APIs are wrapped once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise and a tagged error. Call that wrapper here (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Effect code has no async functions. Return an Effect, or wrap the Promise API in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Read configuration in src/config only: expose it as a service with a layer there (AppConfig.layer), and yield* it where it is needed (STANDARD.md#effect-config).

Name a reusable Effect.fn after its variable: const getUser = Effect.fn("getUser")(function* ...). Use Effect.fnUntraced when it is not a useful tracing span (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Do not throw inside Effect code: a throw becomes an untyped defect. Fail with a typed error: return yield* new SomeError({...}) (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }, { httpApiStatus }). HttpApi can then encode them and the typed client can decode them (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Fail with a Schema.TaggedError, not a bare Error, so callers can catchTag it and HttpApi can map it to a status (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }), not by extending Error (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).

Declare the real schema. The endpoint schema validates input, encodes output, and generates OpenAPI and the typed client (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).
Keep the message constant and put values in fields: Effect.logInfo("price served").pipe(Effect.annotateLogs({ ticker })) (STANDARD.md#effect-logging).
Effect.promise turns a rejection into a defect. Wrap the Promise API once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch: (cause) => new SomeError({ cause }) }) (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
The service has one HttpApi, in src/data/api/Api.ts. Add your group to it there (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Groups and endpoints live in src/data/api/<group>/<Group>Api.ts, one group per file (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Errors live in an errors.ts file: src/data/api/<group>/errors.ts for errors on the wire, src/features/<name>/errors.ts for internal ones (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Handlers live in src/features/<group>/handlers.ts, named after the group they implement (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Give every service its production layer as static readonly layer, so src/app wires X.layer and tests swap in another static layer (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once, and tests may run effects. Everywhere else, return the Effect (STANDARD.md#effect-running).

A ManagedRuntime bridges Effect into non-Effect code. Build it once in src/app (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Provide layers once, in src/app. Below it, declare what you need with yield* SomeService and compose layers with Layer.provide (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Promise APIs are wrapped once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise and a tagged error. Call that wrapper here (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Effect code has no async functions. Return an Effect, or wrap the Promise API in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Read configuration in src/config only: expose it as a service with a layer there (AppConfig.layer), and yield* it where it is needed (STANDARD.md#effect-config).

Do not .pipe an Effect.fn. Pass the combinators as extra arguments: Effect.fn("name")(function* () {...}, Effect.catchTag(...)) (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Name a reusable Effect.fn after its variable: const getUser = Effect.fn("getUser")(function* ...). Use Effect.fnUntraced when it is not a useful tracing span (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Do not throw inside Effect code: a throw becomes an untyped defect. Fail with a typed error: return yield* new SomeError({...}) (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }, { httpApiStatus }). HttpApi can then encode them and the typed client can decode them (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Fail with a Schema.TaggedError, not a bare Error, so callers can catchTag it and HttpApi can map it to a status (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).

Declare the real schema. The endpoint schema validates input, encodes output, and generates OpenAPI and the typed client (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).

The service has one HttpApi, in src/data/api/Api.ts. Add your group to it there (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Groups and endpoints live in src/data/api/<group>/<Group>Api.ts, one group per file (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).

Handlers live in src/features/<group>/handlers.ts, named after the group they implement (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Give every service its production layer as static readonly layer, so src/app wires X.layer and tests swap in another static layer (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once, and tests may run effects. Everywhere else, return the Effect (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
A ManagedRuntime bridges Effect into non-Effect code. Build it once in src/app (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Provide layers once, in src/app. Below it, declare what you need with yield* SomeService and compose layers with Layer.provide (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Promise APIs are wrapped once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise and a tagged error. Call that wrapper here (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Effect code has no async functions. Return an Effect, or wrap the Promise API in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Read configuration in src/config only: expose it as a service with a layer there (AppConfig.layer), and yield* it where it is needed (STANDARD.md#effect-config).

Do not .pipe an Effect.fn. Pass the combinators as extra arguments: Effect.fn("name")(function* () {...}, Effect.catchTag(...)) (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Name a reusable Effect.fn after its variable: const getUser = Effect.fn("getUser")(function* ...). Use Effect.fnUntraced when it is not a useful tracing span (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Do not throw inside Effect code: a throw becomes an untyped defect. Fail with a typed error: return yield* new SomeError({...}) (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }, { httpApiStatus }). HttpApi can then encode them and the typed client can decode them (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).

Import the module as a namespace: import * as Effect from "effect/Effect" (or import type * as ...). One import style, and every call reads Module.fn (STANDARD.md#effect-imports).
Use Effect.fn("name")(function* (...) { ... }) instead of a function that only returns Effect.gen. It names the span and keeps stack traces (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Use Effect.fn("name")(function* (...) { ... }) instead of a function that only returns Effect.gen. It names the span and keeps stack traces (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Use Effect.fn("name")(function* (...) { ... }) instead of a function that only returns Effect.gen. It names the span and keeps stack traces (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Do not .pipe an Effect.fn. Pass the combinators as extra arguments: Effect.fn("name")(function* () {...}, Effect.catchTag(...)) (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Do not .pipe an Effect.fn. Pass the combinators as extra arguments: Effect.fn("name")(function* () {...}, Effect.catchTag(...)) (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Name a reusable Effect.fn after its variable: const getUser = Effect.fn("getUser")(function* ...). Use Effect.fnUntraced when it is not a useful tracing span (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Do not throw inside Effect code: a throw becomes an untyped defect. Fail with a typed error: return yield* new SomeError({...}) (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }, { httpApiStatus }). HttpApi can then encode them and the typed client can decode them (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Fail with a Schema.TaggedError, not a bare Error, so callers can catchTag it and HttpApi can map it to a status (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Define errors with Schema.TaggedError<E>()("E", { ...fields }), not by extending Error (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchAll is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catch (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchAllCause is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchCause (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchAllDefect is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchDefect (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchSome is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchFilter (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.catchSomeCause is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.catchCauseFilter (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.fork is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.forkChild (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Effect.forkDaemon is the v3 name. In v4 it is Effect.forkDetach (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
v4 services use Context.Service<Self, Shape>()("package/path/Name") (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
v4 services use Context.Service<Self, Shape>()("package/path/Name"), with a static layer built by Layer.effect (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Give the service a global identifier with the package and folder path: "my-service/features/prices/Prices" (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Declare the real schema. The endpoint schema validates input, encodes output, and generates OpenAPI and the typed client (STANDARD.md#effect-http-api).
Keep the message constant and put values in fields: Effect.logInfo("price served").pipe(Effect.annotateLogs({ ticker })) (STANDARD.md#effect-logging).
Effect.promise turns a rejection into a defect. Wrap the Promise API once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise({ try, catch: (cause) => new SomeError({ cause }) }) (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Groups and endpoints live in src/data/api/<group>/<Group>Api.ts, one group per file (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Errors live in an errors.ts file: src/data/api/<group>/errors.ts for errors on the wire, src/features/<name>/errors.ts for internal ones (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Handlers live in src/features/<group>/handlers.ts, named after the group they implement (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Give every service its production layer as static readonly layer, so src/app wires X.layer and tests swap in another static layer (STANDARD.md#effect-api-layout).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once, and tests may run effects. Everywhere else, return the Effect (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Run effects only at the edge: src/app/main.ts calls runMain once (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
A ManagedRuntime bridges Effect into non-Effect code. Build it once in src/app (STANDARD.md#effect-running).
Provide layers once, in src/app. Below it, declare what you need with yield* SomeService and compose layers with Layer.provide (STANDARD.md#effect-services).
Promise APIs are wrapped once in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise and a tagged error. Call that wrapper here (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Effect code has no async functions. Return an Effect, or wrap the Promise API in @/platform with Effect.tryPromise (STANDARD.md#effect-platform).
Read configuration in src/config only: expose it as a service with a layer there (AppConfig.layer), and yield* it where it is needed (STANDARD.md#effect-config).

This effect is built and dropped, so it never runs. Write yield* in front of it, or chain it with Effect.andThen / Effect.tap (STANDARD.md#effect-style).
Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).

A ManagedRuntime bridges Effect into non-Effect code. Build it once in src/app (STANDARD.md#effect-running).

Write return yield* new SomeError(...), so TypeScript knows the generator stops here (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
Do not throw inside Effect code: a throw becomes an untyped defect. Fail with a typed error: return yield* new SomeError({...}) (STANDARD.md#effect-errors).
